gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the xTool M2, which ChatGPT named best overall for beginners, runs only in xTool Studio: xTool's own M2 FAQ says it is not compatible with LightBurn or XCS, LightBurn's device list marks the M2 'Unsupported', and its modules and accessories are locked to the M2.
standout_why: Maker-wise (cited) says only 'xTool and Glowforge work best in their own apps' and never says which machines LightBurn supports, so it does not state the M2 exclusion. I could not read the cited xTool beginner guide or Tom's Hardware: both came back truncated to their titles. ChatGPT's own answer calls the Falcon A1 'LightBurn compatible' and gives the M2 no software caveat. That suggests its sources did not state the M2 is excluded, but I can't rule out that xTool's or Tom's page mentions it somewhere.
decides: This confirms the M2 for a beginner who will stay in one simple app. It moves a buyer who wants LightBurn (to run more than one machine, use Linux, or follow LightBurn tutorials) to the Creality Falcon A1, A1C or A1 Pro. Creality's wiki publishes LightBurn device files for the A1C and A1 Pro, and CNX Software ran the A1 Pro with LightBurn and LaserGRBL listed as supported. The M2's upgrade path is also closed: other xTool modules don't fit it, and only the RA3 Lite rotary and the M2 Riser Base Kit are listed for it.

findings.label: Compatible software
findings.value: xTool Studio only (Windows/macOS); 'xTool M2 is not compatible with LightBurn or XCS.'
findings.source_title: xTool M2 FAQ - xTool Support Center (updated Nov 5, 2026)
findings.note: Maker FAQ. Connection is USB or Wi-Fi, controlled from a PC. iPad, Android and Chromebook are not listed.

findings.label: LightBurn device support
findings.value: M2: No, 'Unsupported' (M1 and M1 Ultra also unsupported; S1, F1, D1 and P2S supported)
findings.note: LightBurn's own detailed xTool device support table. It agrees with the maker FAQ.

findings.label: Module cross-compatibility
findings.value: M2 takes 10W/20W/40W diode, 3W IR and CMYK inkjet modules. Processing modules from other xTool machines don't fit. No blade cutting. No conveyor feeder.
findings.source_title: xTool M2 FAQ - xTool Support Center
findings.note: The FAQ also says 'Accessories not listed here are not compatible with xTool M2.' M1 Ultra slats do fit.

findings.label: Power adapter by module
findings.value: 10W, 3W IR and inkjet: 25 V 4.8 A; 20W: 25 V 6 A; 40W: 25 V 8 A
findings.source_title: xTool M2 FAQ - xTool Support Center
findings.note: The 10W machine's adapter is rated below what the 20W and 40W modules need. The FAQ doesn't say whether the $899 40W module ships with an 8 A adapter.

findings.label: Rotary, riser and purifier pairings
findings.value: Rotary: xTool RA3 Lite (listed as exclusive). Riser: M2 Riser Base Kit with honeycomb. xTool Desktop Smoke Purifier needs an adapter. AP2, AP2 Max, IF2 and IF2 2.0 are listed as general accessories.
findings.source_title: xTool M2 FAQ - xTool Support Center
findings.note: RA2 Pro isn't listed for the M2. The FAQ says M2 is Class 1 but doesn't say whether that holds with the riser installed.

findings.source_title: xTool M2 Color Craft Laser Cutter & Engraver

findings.label: LightBurn
findings.value: Creality wiki publishes a LightBurn connection guide with an A1C device profile (creality_falcon_a1c.lbdev)
findings.note: I opened the page and its title confirmed the LightBurn guide, but the body loads by JavaScript and didn't render. The profile file name comes from the search index of this page, so check it before quoting the file name.

findings.label: Price and modules, Creality Falcon US store
findings.value: $269 (list $299), 5W or 10W with AI camera. A1C-specific 10W diode and 1.2W IR modules are listed.
findings.source_title: Creality Falcon A1C Laser Engraver with AI Camera
findings.note: The page says 'Supports rotary engraving' but doesn't say which rotary kit fits the A1C.

findings.label: Software and OS
findings.value: Works with LightBurn and LaserGRBL on Windows and macOS. Falcon Design Space v1.8.1 runs on Windows, macOS, Android and iOS. Connects over USB-C or Wi-Fi. Has a rotary port.
findings.source_title: Creality Falcon A1 Pro Review (CNX Software, Jean-Luc Aufranc, Feb 15, 2026)
findings.note: Jean-Luc Aufranc (CNX Software): 'no Linux support unless using the LightBurn software.' He used Falcon Design Space, not LightBurn, and didn't test the rotary or the 2W IR module.

unsourced: Falcon A1 (10W) LightBurn support on a Creality page: the A1 product page returned HTTP 429 three times and the wiki body renders by JavaScript. The LightBurn forum thread (staff, Oct 2025) only implies A1 use in LightBurn.
Whether Creality's Rotary Kit Pro or RC2 fits the Falcon A1C: the A1C page says 'supports rotary engraving' but names no kit for it.
Price of the xTool RA3 Lite rotary for the M2 on xtool.com: not checked because xTool returned HTTP 429.
Laser wattage of the $499 xTool M2 variant: the product page returned HTTP 429.
Whether the M2 stays Class 1 with the Riser Base Kit: xTool's S1 riser listing says it voids Class 1, but the M2 FAQ is silent on this.
What the cited xTool beginner guide and Tom's Hardware say about LightBurn and accessories: both fetches came back truncated to the page titles.
